## Purpose and completion criteria

Assess the external migration feature.

| Measure | Comparison | Acceptance criterion |
|---|---|---|
| Accounting and implementation | Existing tests | Successful unit tests |

## Overview of Design




## Simulation Test

We will keep the rest of the simulation simple for now with static fertility, mortality, and on demand union formation. However, I will add race and region as variables so I can get one variable whose ancestry is tracked in sim and one whose ancestry is not tracked. The immigrant template population(s) will need to match the race groups but will not need to contain region, but will have to have an assignment made.

First, lets just sim a pop with the basics and no regional transitions for 100 years to get a good starting pop.

We are going to track generation through the group mechanism, so I am going to add that here, even though it won't become relevant until later.

1   1      2
1   1.5    2
1   2      2.5
1   2.5    2.5
1   3+     2.5
1.5 1.5    2
1.5 2
1.5 2.5
1.5 3
2   2      3
2   2.5
2   3 
2.5 3


```{r}

inheritance_gen <- group_inheritance(
  method = "custom",
  fun = function(mother_group, father_group) {
    
  }
)

increment_gen <- function(gen) {
  
  if (gen %in% c("1", "1.5")) {
    return("2")
  }

  return("3+")
}

grp_gen <- group(
  categories =c("1", "1.5", "2", "2.5", "3+"), 
  inheritance = group_inheritance(
    method = "custom",
    fun = function(mother_group, father_group) {
      if(is.na(father_group) || (mother_group == father_group)) {
        return(increment_gen(mother_group))
      }

    

    }
  )
)

```

```{r}

# allow race exogamy to vary across combinations
race_exogamy <- c(
"White:Black" = -4,
  "White:Asian" = -2,
  "White:Latino" = -1.5,
  "Black:Asian" = -4,
  "Black:Latino" = -3,
  "Asian:Latino" = -2
)

# for birthplace, all non-same birthplace cases get the same value
birthplace_exogamy <- c(
  "native:asia" = -0.7,
  "native:latin_america" = -0.7,
  "asia:latin_america" = -0.7
)

```




```{r}
#| label: setup-starting-pop


model <- hammel_model() |>
  set_fertility(usa_2000_fertility) |>
  set_mortality(usa_2000_mortality) |>
  set_union_formation(
    "on_demand",
    matching = age_gap_matching_model(
      3, 5, 
      group_exogamy = list(
        region = NA,
        race = race_exogamy
      )
    )
  ) |>
  set_groups(
    race = group(
      categories = c("White", "Black", "Asian", "Latino"),
      ancestry = TRUE,
      inheritance = "ancestry"
    ),
    region = group(
      categories = c("NE", "MW", "S", "W")
    )
  )

# start with no Asian or Latino members
region_race_dist <- tibble::tribble(
  ~race, ~region, ~weight,
 "White",   "NE",    0.166,
 "White",   "MW",    0.216,
 "White",   "S",     0.294,
 "White",   "W",     0.174,
 "Black",   "NE",    0.025,
 "Black",   "MW",    0.026,
 "Black",   "S",     0.077,
 "Black",   "W",     0.022,
 "Asian",   "NE",    0.000,
 "Asian",   "MW",    0.000,
 "Asian",   "S",     0.000,
 "Asian",   "W",     0.000,
 "Latino",  "NE",    0.000,
 "Latino",  "MW",    0.000,
 "Latino",  "S",     0.000,
 "Latino",  "W",     0.000
)

model <- model |>
  set_population(generate_uniform_population(50000, groups = region_race_dist))

pop_start <- run_simulation(model, 100, 42, progress = interactive())
summary(pop_start)

model <- model |>
  set_population(pop_start)
```

Ok, so now lets set up two template populations: one from Latin America and one from Asia.

```{r}
# Use Taiwan
mortality_taiwan <- get_mortality_hmd("TWN", 1980, shape = "5x1", open_age = 85)
fertility_taiwan <- get_fertility_hfd("TWN", 1976)

model_asian_template <- hammel_model() |>
  set_fertility(fertility_taiwan) |>
  set_mortality(mortality_taiwan) |>
  set_union_formation("on_demand") |>
  set_population(
    generate_uniform_population(
      20000,
      groups = list(race = c(White = 0, Black = 0, Asian = 1, Latino = 0))
    )
  )

pop_asian_template <- run_simulation(model_asian_template, 100, 42, progress = interactive())
summary(pop_asian_template)
```

```{r}
# use Chile
mortality_chile <- get_mortality_hmd("CHL", 1992, shape = "5x1", open_age = 85)
fertility_chile <- get_fertility_hfd("CHL", 1992)

model_latino_template <- hammel_model() |>
  set_fertility(fertility_chile) |>
  set_mortality(mortality_chile) |>
  set_union_formation("on_demand") |>
  set_population(
    generate_uniform_population(
      30000,
      groups = list(race = c(White = 0, Black = 0, Asian = 0, Latino = 1))
    )
  )

pop_latino_template <- run_simulation(model_latino_template, 100, 42, progress = interactive())
summary(pop_latino_template)
```

Ok, now lets add the migration streams.

```{r}

# custom weight model to highly select working age pop
migrant_selection_fun <- weight_model(fun = function(members, bin) {
  w <- ifelse(
    members$age >= 20 & members$age < 45, 1,
    ifelse(members$age >= 45 & members$age < 65, 0.3,
      ifelse(members$age >= 65, 0.05, 0.02))
  )
  w <- ifelse(members$sex == "m", 2 * w, w)
  log(w)
})

model <- model |>
  set_immigration(
    birthplace_ancestry = TRUE,
    asia = immigration_stream(
      pop_asian_template,
      intensity = 200,
      assignment = list(
        region = migrant_assignment(
          "probability", probs = c("NE" = 0.3, "MW" = 0.15, "S" = 0.15, "W" = 0.4)
        )
      ),
      household = household(),
      weights = migrant_selection_fun
    ),
    latin_america = immigration_stream(
      pop_latino_template,
      intensity = 600,
      assignment = list(
        region = migrant_assignment(
          "probability", probs = c("NE" = 0.25, "MW" = 0.2, "S" = 0.2, "W" = 0.35)
        )
      ),
      household = household(),
      weights = migrant_selection_fun
    )
  ) |>
  # redo union formation for new exogamy
  set_union_formation(
    "on_demand",
    matching = age_gap_matching_model(
      3, 5, 
      group_exogamy = list(
        region = NA,
        race = race_exogamy,
        birthplace = birthplace_exogamy
      )
    )
  )

pop_end <- run_simulation(model, 50, 42, progress = interactive())
summary(pop_end)
```

```{r}

# get flows
pop_end$persons |>
  filter(!is.na(arrival_time)) |>
  mutate(arrival_year = floor(arrival_time)) |>
  count(birthplace, arrival_year) |>
  #pivot_wider(id_cols = arrival_year, names_from = stream, values_from = n) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = arrival_year, y = n, color = birthplace))+
  geom_line()+
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(200, 600), linetype = 2)+
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA))

```


```{r}

pop_end |>
  calculate_fertility_rates(
    time_breaks = c(100, 150),
    age_breaks = seq(15, 45, 5),
    conf_level = 0.95
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_start + 2.5, y = rate_fertility))+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), color = NA, fill = "grey70")+
  geom_point(size = 0.5)+
  geom_line(data = usa_2000_fertility, aes(y = rate), linetype = 2, color = "red")
```

```{r}

pop_end |>
  calculate_mortality_rates(
    time_breaks = c(100, 150),
    age_breaks = c(0, 1, seq(5, 100, 5)),
    conf_level = 0.95
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = age_start + 2.5, y = rate_mortality))+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), color = NA, fill = "grey70")+
  geom_point(size = 0.5)+
  geom_line(data = usa_2000_mortality, aes(y = rate), linetype = 2, color = "red")+
  facet_wrap(~sex)+
  scale_y_log10()
```

pop_end$persons |>

```{r}

temp <- inner_join(pop_end$persons, pop_end$ancestry$birthplace)
temp |> 
  mutate(birth_year = floor(birth_time)) |>
  group_by(birth_year, birthplace) |>
  summarize(pct_native = mean(native)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = birth_year, y = pct_native, color = birthplace))+

temp |> 
  mutate(birth_year = floor(birth_time)) |>
  group_by(birth_year, race) |>
  summarize(pct_native = mean(native)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = birth_year, y = pct_native, color = race))+

```
